PAPERS.title: Air pollution exposure in Generation Scotland and long-term health outcomes
PAPERS.short: Generation Scotland EMEP4UK CTM eight pollutants 18 y Cox dementia MI APOE4 low-pollution setting
PAPERS.pm: EMEP4UK chemical transport model annual residential PM2.5, PM10, fine and coarse nitrate, NO, NO2, O3, SO2 at recruitment postcode (365 d before baseline)
PAPERS.endpoint: Incident hypertension, IHD, MI, stroke and all-cause dementia over 18 y
PAPERS.affil: University of Edinburgh, UK; University of Edinburgh, UK
PAPERS.n: Generation Scotland, 22,071 adults recruited 2006-2011, followed 18 years; annual residential exposures from the EMEP4UK chemical transport model for eight pollutants, Cox models for five non-communicable outcomes. Above-average annual PM2.5 was associated with all-cause dementia (HR 1.48, 95% CI 1.15-1.90) and coarse nitrate with MI (HR 1.79, 1.25-2.56); one APOE e4 allele raised the PM10-dementia HR to 2.38 (1.36-4.16). 99% of participants exceeded the WHO 2021 24-h PM2.5 guideline despite a low-pollution setting. The contrast is a dichotomy at the mean, not a per-increment slope, eight pollutants by five outcomes invite multiplicity, and a single baseline postcode ignores 18 years of residential mobility. Relevance: CTM-only exposure at postcode scale; low-cost networks could test whether the dichotomy survives measured within-city gradients.

PAPERS.title: Assessing satellite and reanalysis PM(2.5) datasets for air quality applications in India.
PAPERS.short: India CAMS EAC4 MERRA-2 SatPM2.5 V6.GL vs 249 CPCB stations 2022-2023 bias correction holdout
PAPERS.pm: CAMS EAC4, MERRA-2 and satellite-derived SatPM2.5 V6.GL.02.04 versus quality-controlled CPCB regulatory PM2.5, 0.75 deg common grid
PAPERS.endpoint: Product bias, RMSE, IOA and daily 60 ug/m3 exceedance frequency
PAPERS.affil: National Atmospheric Research Laboratory, India; Indian Institute of Space Science and Technology, India
PAPERS.n: Evaluates three gridded PM2.5 products against 248-249 CPCB stations aggregated into 101 CAMS cells, 2022-2023. Monthly: SatPM2.5 MB -2.07 ug/m3, RMSE 25.34, r 0.708; MERRA-2 MB -6.83, RMSE 27.58; CAMS MB +56.15, RMSE 79.39 ug/m3. Daily RMSE 85.16 (CAMS) and 35.12 (MERRA-2). Spatiotemporal holdout correction cut CAMS daily RMSE from 84.53 to 33.23 ug/m3 (IOA 0.580 to 0.781). Observed exceedance of 60 ug/m3 on 27.0% of cell-days versus 64.6% raw CAMS and 20.0% raw MERRA-2. Weakness: validation at 0.75 deg against a monitor network clustered in cities, so rural error and the satellite product daily skill are not characterised. Relevance: high - quantifies the reference error any satellite-LCS fusion inherits in India.

PAPERS.title: Global probabilistic forecasting of air pollution at the kilometre scale
PAPERS.short: Foehn generative ML global km-scale PM2.5 ensemble forecast vs operational CAMS 4-day lead extremes
PAPERS.pm: Global kilometre-scale PM2.5 estimates as training target; generative ensemble with source-region attribution
PAPERS.endpoint: Station-level forecast skill and detection of local PM2.5 extremes
PAPERS.affil: LUT University, Finland; LUT University, Finland
PAPERS.n: Preprint introducing Foehn, a generative model trained on global kilometre-scale PM2.5 estimates that also computes where the air comes from. Over a year of retrospective forecasts it beat the operational forecast at three of four stations, its ensembles were calibrated, and the ensemble mean detected local pollution extremes four days ahead as well as the operational system did one day ahead. No skill metrics, station counts or regional breakdown are given in the abstract, and the authors concede the method needs kilometre-scale data in real time, which do not yet exist. Training on a modelled km-scale product means errors in that product are learned as truth. Relevance: high conceptually - dense low-cost networks are the obvious real-time km-scale input the model says it lacks.

PAPERS.title: Do Traffic Congestion Indicators Improve PM2.5 Forecasting? Evidence from Machine Learning Models in Kampala
PAPERS.short: Kampala AirQo LCS PM2.5 Google Routes congestion RF HistGBR forecasting no gain
PAPERS.pm: Hourly PM2.5, temperature and humidity from the AirQo low-cost monitoring network; congestion from Google Routes API
PAPERS.endpoint: Hourly PM2.5 forecast MAE, RMSE, R2
PAPERS.affil: Victoria University, Uganda; Victoria University, Uganda
PAPERS.n: Preprint: 696 hourly observations from an AirQo low-cost PM2.5 node on Jinja Road, Kampala, paired with Google Routes speed, travel duration and a traffic performance index. The best environmental baseline (HistGradientBoosting) reached MAE 15.28, RMSE 21.40, R2 0.575; the best traffic-enhanced model was worse (MAE 23.16, RMSE 31.70, R2 0.475); adding lagged PM2.5 gave R2 0.625. Congestion indicators added no predictive value beyond meteorology and time. 29 days of data from one corridor cannot separate traffic from diurnal structure, the LCS calibration status is not stated, and a degraded score after adding features points to overfitting rather than absent traffic signal. Relevance: direct - an LCS network used as the forecasting target in a data-poor African city.

PAPERS.title: Changes in air pollution-avoidance behaviour and blood pressure following an AirHealth behavioural intervention among adults in Nigeria: a quasi-experimental study.
PAPERS.short: Ibadan AirHealth co-created behavioural intervention COM-B avoidance SBP pre-post 607 adults
PAPERS.pm: No PM measurement; air-pollution-avoidance behaviour by 11-item COM-B score
PAPERS.endpoint: Systolic and diastolic blood pressure; avoidance-behaviour score
PAPERS.affil: Osun State University, Nigeria; University of Ibadan, Nigeria
PAPERS.n: Pre-post quasi-experiment in 607 apparently healthy, highly exposed adults in Ibadan; 12-week co-created AirHealth intervention (video documentary plus community education). Mean SBP fell by 4.58 mmHg (95% CI 1.43-7.74); DBP change was not significant. Unimproved avoidance behaviour predicted unimproved BP (aOR 2.87, 1.87-3.80). There is no control group, no exposure measurement and baseline SBP SD of 30.6 mmHg, so regression to the mean, seasonality and white-coat effects cannot be excluded, and nothing ties the BP change to reduced PM dose. Relevance: indirect - the trial needs exactly the personal or community sensor layer it lacks to show behaviour changed exposure.

PAPERS.title: Climate-specific short-term associations between ambient temperature, air pollution, and acute myocardial infarction in Israel.
PAPERS.short: Israel Rambam Soroka 2000-2018 time-series AMI temperature NO2 PM2.5 PM10 Mediterranean vs semi-arid
PAPERS.pm: Daily ambient PM2.5, PM10, NO2, O3 with lags 0-3 d; source of exposure not stated in abstract
PAPERS.endpoint: Daily AMI hospitalisations
PAPERS.affil: Ben-Gurion University of the Negev, Israel; Rambam Healthcare Campus, Israel
PAPERS.n: Two-hospital time-series, 2000-2018: 18,229 AMI admissions in Mediterranean northern Israel and 30,208 in semi-arid southern Israel; Poisson/negative-binomial GLMs with lags to 3 days. Temperature dominates: higher Tmax lowered AMI risk in the north (lag 2 IRR 0.991, 0.986-0.997) and raised it in southern summers (lag 1 IRR 1.031, 1.011-1.050). The abstract reports only "small but statistically significant" associations for PM2.5 and NO2 in the north and none in the south, with no PM effect size, increment or CI. Single-hospital catchments and unstated monitor assignment limit exposure accuracy, and desert-dust PM10 is not separated. Relevance: low - the PM result is unquantified; climate-specific effect modification is the transferable point.

PAPERS.title: Air Pollution and Primary Myocardial Infarction: An Ecological Study in a Low-Risk European Region
PAPERS.short: Madrid metro 2013-2018 CP-STEMI 4406 cases quasi-Poisson IDW monitors PM2.5
PAPERS.pm: Municipal daily PM2.5, PM10, NO2 and others from inverse-distance-weighted regulatory stations to municipality centroid
PAPERS.endpoint: ST-elevation MI with angiographically demonstrated culprit plaque
PAPERS.affil: not stated in record; not stated in record
PAPERS.n: Preprint, Madrid metropolitan area 2013-2018: 4,406 culprit-plaque STEMI cases (CP-STEMI) linked by municipality to inverse-distance-weighted daily station data; quasi-Poisson regression on prior-day exposures. The authors conclude an increased CP-STEMI risk independently associated with PM2.5 and a cold effect, but the results section of the abstract is truncated after "Particulate matter", so no estimate, lag or CI is available. NO2 exceeded the WHO level on more than half of days. Strengths: a tight case definition that reduces outcome misclassification. Weaknesses: centroid-IDW exposure for whole municipalities and an ecological design. Relevance: moderate - IDW from a sparse network is the exposure step a dense LCS mesh would replace.

PAPERS.title: The Air We Breathe: Utilizing Local Environmental Monitoring to Direct Allergy Care.
PAPERS.short: Colorado review monitoring for allergy care regulatory networks pollen community sensors personal monitors EHR
PAPERS.pm: Regulatory networks, pollen surveillance, community sensor networks, models, indoor and personal monitors
PAPERS.endpoint: Allergic disease management (clinical integration of exposure data)
PAPERS.affil: University of Colorado Anschutz, USA; University of Colorado Anschutz, USA
PAPERS.n: Narrative review for allergists of the exposure-data options available to clinical practice: regulatory air-quality networks, pollen surveillance, community low-cost sensor networks, modelling tools, and indoor and personal monitors. It weighs evidence for clinical relevance and sets out practical routes to integrate exposure data into patient-centred care, naming data validation, workflow integration and EHR interoperability as the barriers. No new data or quantitative synthesis; the abstract gives no criteria for when sensor data are trustworthy enough to act on. Relevance: direct - one of few clinical reviews that treats community LCS networks as a care input, and it frames validation as the gating problem.

PAPERS.title: A Decadal Assessment of PM2.5 Pollution in Dhaka, Bangladesh (2015-2024): Pollution Severity, Temporal Variability, and Meteorological Associations
PAPERS.short: Dhaka 2015-2024 three stations PM2.5 annual 77-109 ug/m3 seasonality GLM no trend
PAPERS.pm: Daily PM2.5 from three Dhaka regulatory monitoring stations with meteorology
PAPERS.endpoint: Annual and seasonal PM2.5 levels, trend, meteorological correlates
PAPERS.affil: not stated in record; not stated in record
PAPERS.n: Preprint analysing 7,943 station-days (6,268 valid) from three Dhaka stations, 2015-2024. Annual means ranged from 77.24 ug/m3 (2017) to 108.74 ug/m3 (2021), 15-22 times the WHO annual guideline; winter exceeded monsoon (p<0.001); interannual differences were significant (GLM p=0.033) but no linear trend was found (p=0.797). Temperature, RH and wind were negatively correlated with PM2.5 bivariately but not significant after adjustment. Data completeness of 79% with no statement on gap structure, three stations for a megacity, and linear regression on annual means are weak tools for trend detection. Relevance: moderate - three regulatory sites for over 20 million people is the coverage gap that LCS networks in Dhaka are meant to close.

PAPERS.title: Atmospheric trace elements in PM(2.5) at a regional background site in the western Himalaya: source identification and risk implications.
PAPERS.short: Kashmir western Himalaya background 2019 SASS Teflon ED-XRF PM2.5 trace elements PCA crustal combustion risk
PAPERS.pm: 24-h integrated PM2.5 on Teflon filters (SASS), alternate days 2019, elements by ED-XRF
PAPERS.endpoint: PM2.5 elemental composition, PCA sources, inhalation/dermal/ingestion risk
PAPERS.affil: University of Kashmir, India; University of Kashmir, India
PAPERS.n: First year-long PM2.5 elemental record from a western Himalayan background site: 24-h SASS Teflon samples on alternate days through 2019, ED-XRF. Trace elements were about 11% of PM2.5 mass, crustal elements dominating in summer and autumn; Zn > Cu > Mn > Pb > V > Cr. PCA attributed 50.8% of variance to crustal sources, 19.9% to combustion and 8.4% to vehicles. Cr(VI) drove inhalation cancer risk (4.0e-7 adults, 1.0e-7 children); all HQ below 1. Data are seven years old, PCA variance shares are not mass apportionment, and treating Cr as Cr(VI) is untested. Relevance: low-moderate - composition at a site where optical LCS would face a dust-dominated, hygroscopically different aerosol.

PAPERS.title: An Automated QGIS Plugin to Generate ENVI-met Traffic Emission Sources from Vehicle Trajectories
PAPERS.short: Mainz QGIS plugin SUMO trajectories to ENVI-met line sources Berlin traffic station PM2.5 R2 0.94 footprint
PAPERS.pm: ENVI-met V6 street-canyon PM2.5, PM10 and NOx from segment-specific traffic line sources plus background forcing
PAPERS.endpoint: Agreement of modelled with measured street-level PM and NOx increment
PAPERS.affil: Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz, Germany; Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz, Germany
PAPERS.n: Preprint describing an open-source QGIS plugin that converts vehicle trajectories into street-segment ENVI-met line sources with hourly emission profiles. Tested with SUMO-generated passenger-car trajectories at an official Berlin traffic station over six summer and autumn days: R2 0.94 for PM2.5 and 0.82 for PM10, "largely through the background", and 71% of the measured local NOx increment; a backward Lagrangian footprint localised the signal to the adjacent canyon. The PM agreement is mostly inherited from background forcing, so the tool performance for the local traffic PM increment is not demonstrated, and six days at one site is thin. Relevance: moderate - microscale models like this are what LCS street-level data would validate.

PAPERS.title: Phytobarriers reduce the dispersion of particulate matter associated with potentially toxic elements
PAPERS.short: Mexico City Penon-Texcoco roads phytobarrier index washed vs unwashed leaves Tamarix Eucalyptus ESEM PM10
PAPERS.pm: Leaf-deposited particles (washed vs unwashed leaf PTE content) and ESEM particle sizing; no airborne PM concentration
PAPERS.endpoint: Phytobarrier index for Pb, Cd, Zn, Mn retention by roadside species
PAPERS.affil: Colegio de Postgraduados, Mexico; Colegio de Postgraduados, Mexico
PAPERS.n: Preprint sampling soil and leaves at 26 roadside sites along the Penon-Texcoco and Anillo Periferico roads, Mexico. A phytobarrier index from washed versus unwashed leaf PTE concentrations showed consistently higher Pb, Cd, Zn and Mn on unwashed leaves; ESEM showed deposited particles predominantly below 10 um. Tamarix sp. and Eucalyptus sp. retained most particles. Soil means: Pb 27.8, Cd 1.3, Zn 140, Mn 278 mg/kg. No airborne PM was measured upwind or downwind, so the claim that vegetation reduces PM dispersion is inferred from leaf loading, not shown. Relevance: low - mitigation claim that needs paired upwind/downwind sensor transects to test.

PAPERS.title: Intercomparison of nighttime aerosol optical depth retrievals from both reflectance-based and city light-based methods using VIIRS DNB data
PAPERS.short: VIIRS DNB nighttime AOD lunar reflectance vs city-light retrieval Dakar AERONET MODIS 2017-2019
PAPERS.pm: Nighttime aerosol optical depth from VIIRS Day/Night Band by lunar-reflectance and artificial-light methods
PAPERS.endpoint: Agreement with solar and lunar AERONET AOD and daytime MODIS AOD
PAPERS.affil: University of North Dakota, USA; not stated in record
PAPERS.n: Compares two nighttime AOD retrievals from the VIIRS Day/Night Band over Dakar and Dakar Belair, 2017-2019: a lunar-reflectance method and a city-light method that reads aerosol from the upward diffusion of artificial light. Both were evaluated against solar and lunar AERONET and daytime MODIS. Both showed skill in locating over-ocean plumes and tracked AERONET quantitatively, and combining them raised nighttime sampling by more than 50%. No R2 or bias values are given in the abstract; cloud contamination and lunar-irradiance modelling remain unquantified error sources. Relevance: moderate - nighttime AOD would fill the half of the diurnal cycle that satellite-surface PM fusion currently leaves to sensors alone.

PAPERS.title: Dynamic calibration method for the system constant of high-spectral-resolution lidar with airborne experimental verification.
PAPERS.short: Shanghai airborne HSRL time-varying system constant dynamic calibration roll angle disturbance
PAPERS.pm: Aerosol attenuated backscatter from high-spectral-resolution lidar, ground and airborne
PAPERS.endpoint: Relative error and uncertainty of calibrated HSRL backscatter channels
PAPERS.affil: Shanghai Institute of Optics and Fine Mechanics, China; Shanghai Institute of Optics and Fine Mechanics, China
PAPERS.n: Proposes a time-varying effective system response factor to diagnose and dynamically calibrate the system constant of an airborne high-spectral-resolution lidar, using ground-based stationary observations as the reference. The calibration coefficient drifted even on the ground; in one flight, 62% of significant response-factor variations coincided with platform disturbances, roll angle most often. After dynamic calibration, mean relative errors of the parallel-polarisation and HSR channels fell below 10%, total uncertainty below 5.5%. One flight dataset and no comparison with an independent aerosol reference limit generality. Relevance: low-moderate - the drift-tracking logic is the same problem as LCS baseline drift, one instrument class up.

PAPERS.title: Airborne and marine microplastics in the Northern Indian Ocean: decoupled pathways traced by black carbon
PAPERS.short: Maldives MCOH airborne vs marine microplastics deposition box micro-Raman eBC scattering advection
PAPERS.pm: Airborne microplastics by deposition box (MP m-3) alongside aerosol scattering and equivalent black carbon
PAPERS.endpoint: Airborne and marine microplastic concentration, size, polymer; coupling to eBC
PAPERS.affil: Institute of Oceanology, Polish Academy of Sciences, Poland; not stated in record
PAPERS.n: One-month dry-season campaign at the Maldives Climate Observatory Hanimaadhoo: airborne microplastics by deposition box with optical microscopy and micro-Raman, coastal seawater sampling, plus aerosol scattering and eBC. Airborne MPs 0-10.3 MP m-3 (mean 3.1 +/- 2.8); marine MPs 120-2656 MP m-3. Size and polymer differed between reservoirs, and airborne MP variability tracked polluted advection, elevated eBC and scattering rather than sea spray. A deposition box gives a volumetric concentration only through assumed deposition velocities, and one month cannot test the seasonal sea-spray pathway. Relevance: moderate - eBC and scattering, the quantities low-cost optical sensors approximate, served as tracers for a particle class sensors cannot speciate.

PAPERS.title: Addressing systematic underestimation in a global ship emission inventory through improved fleet representation and fuel compliance characterization
PAPERS.short: Tsinghua SEIMv2.3 near-real-time AIS ship inventory sulfur compliance scrubbers PM2.5 BC underestimation 43%
PAPERS.pm: Global ship PM2.5, BC and CO2 emissions from AIS activity with fuel-sulfur compliance pathways
PAPERS.endpoint: Inventory completeness and PM2.5/BC emission bias
PAPERS.affil: not stated in record; Tsinghua University, China
PAPERS.n: Updates the Ship Emission Inventory Model to SEIMv2.3 with daily ship technical-database updates and explicit post-2020 sulfur-compliance pathways (very-low-sulfur fuel versus scrubbers with heavy fuel oil), producing emissions within 3 days of AIS acquisition. Daily updates uncovered 8% and 6.2% of active bulk-carrier and container gross tonnage, up to 5.4% of global ship CO2. Assuming universal low-sulfur fuel underestimates ship PM2.5 by about 43% and BC by 15%, reaching 56% of PM2.5 in the Indian Ocean. No independent observational check of the corrected emissions is reported. Relevance: indirect - a 43% PM2.5 inventory bias propagates straight into CTM exposure surfaces near ports.

PAPERS.title: Year-round organic aerosol sources in the Po Valley: A comparative study of Bologna and Milan within RI-URBANS
PAPERS.short: Po Valley Bologna Milan 2023 ACSM NR-PM1 variable-factor-number PMF BBOA SOA 75%
PAPERS.pm: Non-refractory PM1 composition by Aerosol Chemical Speciation Monitor at two urban background sites, 2023
PAPERS.endpoint: Organic aerosol factors (HOA, BBOA, LO-OOA, MO-OOA) by season and site
PAPERS.affil: Institute of Atmospheric Sciences and Climate, CNR, Italy; Institute of Atmospheric Sciences and Climate, CNR, Italy
PAPERS.n: Simultaneous year-long (2023) ACSM measurements of NR-PM1 at Bologna and Milan urban background sites, with a new variable-factor-number PMF that constrains biomass-burning OA only when f60 exceeds 0.3%, avoiding warm-season BBOA overestimation. Mean NR-PM1 was 8.02 +/- 8.63 ug/m3 (Bologna) and 8.37 +/- 8.10 (Milan); OA dominated year-round. Primary OA (HOA plus BBOA) was 8-23% of OA; secondary OA exceeded 75%, MO-OOA alone 45-50%. Winter peaks followed stagnation, summer SOA photochemistry. Two sites cannot by themselves establish basin-wide homogeneity, and the f60 threshold is a tuning choice. Relevance: moderate - a regionally homogeneous, SOA-dominated PM1 means low-cost networks in the basin mostly resolve meteorology, not local sources.

PAPERS.title: Ambient PM10 Patterns in Provinces Affected by the 2023 Turkiye Earthquakes: A Descriptive Assessment of 2022-2023 Monitoring Data
PAPERS.short: Turkiye 2023 earthquakes 11 provinces 28 stations PM10 2022 vs 2023 AirQ+ attributable proportion
PAPERS.pm: Daily PM10 from 28 national regulatory monitoring stations, 2022-2023
PAPERS.endpoint: Annual PM10, exceedance days, AirQ+ attributable proportion of all-cause mortality
PAPERS.affil: Istanbul Provincial Health Directorate, Turkiye; Istanbul University-Cerrahpasa, Turkiye
PAPERS.n: Descriptive comparison of daily PM10 from 28 stations in 11 provinces hit by the February 2023 earthquakes, 2023 against 2022. Annual means rose in four provinces and fell in seven; Kahramanmaras rose most (33.0%), Elazig fell most (13.4%). Exceedance days rose from 144 to 218 in Kahramanmaras and 109 to 143 in Hatay. All provinces exceeded the WHO 15 ug/m3 guideline both years; AirQ+ attributable proportion of mortality reached 17.36% against a 40 ug/m3 counterfactual. The authors concede no unaffected comparison provinces and no meteorological adjustment, so nothing is attributable to the earthquake, and stations damaged in the disaster may bias coverage. Relevance: direct - post-disaster demolition dust is where rapidly deployable sensors outperform a damaged fixed network.

PAPERS.title: Distinct Source Signatures of Two Asian Dust Events Revealed by Pb Isotopes in PM10
PAPERS.short: Korea coastal industrial site 2023 Asian dust PM10 Pb isotopes Bayesian mixing Kumtag Gobi
PAPERS.pm: PM10 filter samples March-April 2023, ions, elements and Pb isotope ratios
PAPERS.endpoint: Source contributions to PM10 during Asian dust and non-dust periods
PAPERS.affil: National Institute of Environmental Research, South Korea; National Institute of Environmental Research, South Korea
PAPERS.n: PM10 sampled March-April 2023 at a coastal industrial site in Korea, analysed for ions, elements and Pb isotopes, with Bayesian source apportionment and back trajectories. PM10 averaged 130.5 ug/m3 during Asian dust versus 77.4 during non-dust; 208Pb/206Pb 2.1187 versus 2.0999. The March and April dust events had similar PM10 and chemistry but different isotopes (p<0.01): March weighted to the Kumtag Desert and coal, April to the Gobi and industry. Two events at one site, and Bayesian mixing results depend on end-member libraries not described in the abstract. Relevance: low - isotopic source discrimination is invisible to mass-only sensors, though dust events are a known LCS undercount regime.

PAPERS.title: Landfill mining resuspends buried micro- and nanoplastics as airborne particles.
PAPERS.short: Tongji active landfill mining TSP Andersen impactor airborne micro-nanoplastics hopper PET Gaussian plume inhalation dose
PAPERS.pm: TSP (100 um inlet) and Andersen cascade impactor 0.43-10 um fractions, polymer-resolved micro- and nanoplastics
PAPERS.endpoint: Airborne MNP concentration by process, downwind dispersion, estimated inhalation dose
PAPERS.affil: Tongji University, China; Tongji University, China
PAPERS.n: Field sampling at an active landfill mining site with TSP and size-segregated Andersen impactor samples (0.43-10 um). The hopper process generated the highest airborne micro- and nanoplastic (MNP) concentrations; PET was the most abundant polymer by mass; MNPs made up 0.04-9.9% of 0.43-10 um aerosol mass and co-varied with TSP. A density-corrected Gaussian plume placed maximum concentrations 2.7 m (TSP microplastics) and 4.4 m (aerosol MNPs) downwind, and inhalation exposure was estimated at 16-19,271 ng/kg/day. A single site, no stated sampling duration, and a three-order-of-magnitude dose range show how assumption-driven the exposure estimate is. Relevance: moderate - co-emission with TSP suggests a cheap PM proxy for MNP release at waste sites.

PAPERS.title: Assessing the role of ventilation and indoor air quality in SARS-CoV-2 transmission risk in Belgian nursing homes: the AIR-CO study.
PAPERS.short: AIR-CO Flanders 11 nursing homes 55 rooms CO2 PM2.5 RH ventilation type SARS-CoV-2 air and surface RNA
PAPERS.pm: One-week continuous indoor PM2.5, CO2, temperature and RH per room; instrument not stated in abstract
PAPERS.endpoint: IAQ by ventilation type; environmental SARS-CoV-2 RNA detection
PAPERS.affil: Sciensano, Belgium; Sciensano, Belgium
PAPERS.n: Pilot in 11 Flemish nursing homes, January-May 2022: five rooms each (55 rooms) monitored for one week for CO2, PM2.5, temperature and RH, with one air sample and three surface swabs per room for SARS-CoV-2 RNA. Nine homes had full mechanical ventilation. CO2 mostly stayed within limits; RH was consistently below recommended ranges and temperatures often too high. PM2.5 was comparable across ventilation types, higher in some naturally ventilated spaces; no PM values are given. 61.9% of swabs and 27.5% of air samples were positive, with no consistent link to IAQ parameters. One natural-ventilation home and one week per room give no power for the comparison. Relevance: moderate - continuous PM/CO2 monitoring of care homes is a natural low-cost sensor application.

PAPERS.title: Long-term exposure to air pollution variability and incidence of cardiovascular diseases: Evidence from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS)
PAPERS.short: CHARLS long-term air pollution variability incident CVD (metadata only)
PAPERS.pm: Metadata only - long-term variability of air pollution exposure in CHARLS
PAPERS.endpoint: Metadata only - incident cardiovascular disease
PAPERS.affil: not stated in record
PAPERS.n: Metadata only: no abstract was retrievable from PubMed, Europe PMC or Crossref at issue time. The record (Atmospheric Environment; Ni, Wu, Huang, Ye and colleagues) examines long-term variability in air-pollution exposure, rather than mean level, and incident cardiovascular disease in the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study. No finding is asserted here. Relevance: moderate in principle - exposure variability is a quantity that temporally dense sensor data estimate far better than annual model surfaces.

PAPERS.title: The Acute Exposure Window: A Missing Dimension in Industrial Fire Assessment
PAPERS.short: CNR Italy industrial fire acute exposure window perspective (metadata only)
PAPERS.pm: Metadata only - acute smoke exposure during industrial fires
PAPERS.endpoint: Metadata only - exposure assessment framing for industrial fires
PAPERS.affil: Institute of Clinical Physiology, CNR, Italy; Institute of Bioeconomy, CNR, Italy
PAPERS.n: Metadata only: no abstract was retrievable at issue time. The record (Environmental Science & Technology; Linzalone, Vivani, Zaldei; CNR Institutes of Clinical Physiology and Bioeconomy, Italy) argues that the acute exposure window is missing from industrial fire assessment. No finding is asserted here. Relevance: potentially direct - the last author group has worked on low-cost sensor platforms, and acute fire plumes are the case where rapidly deployed sensors would capture the hours-scale peak that regulatory networks miss.

PAPERS.title: Long-term persistence of radiocesium in house dust following the Fukushima accident: Insights from indoor-outdoor aerosol measurements into deposition fluxes and particle size
PAPERS.short: Fukushima radiocesium house dust indoor-outdoor aerosol deposition particle size (metadata only)
PAPERS.pm: Metadata only - indoor and outdoor aerosol radiocesium, deposition flux and particle size
PAPERS.endpoint: Metadata only - persistence of radiocesium in house dust
PAPERS.affil: not stated in record
PAPERS.n: Metadata only: no abstract was retrievable at issue time. The record (Environment International; Shinohara, Yoshida-Ohuchi) uses indoor-outdoor aerosol measurements to explain the long-term persistence of Fukushima radiocesium in house dust through deposition fluxes and particle size. No finding is asserted here. Relevance: indirect - indoor-outdoor particle transfer and deposition by size is the physics behind indoor/outdoor sensor ratios.

PAPERS.title: Multidimensional comfort evaluation of industrial non-powered air-purifying respirators: integrating facial pressure, thermal responses, breathing resistance and perceived air quality
PAPERS.short: Industrial non-powered respirators comfort facial pressure thermal breathing resistance (metadata only)
PAPERS.pm: Metadata only - respiratory protective equipment against occupational particulates
PAPERS.endpoint: Metadata only - multidimensional respirator comfort
PAPERS.affil: not stated in record
PAPERS.n: Metadata only: no abstract was retrievable at issue time. The record (Building and Environment; Wei, Yin, Yang, Li and colleagues) evaluates the comfort of industrial non-powered air-purifying respirators by facial pressure, thermal response, breathing resistance and perceived air quality. No finding is asserted here. Relevance: indirect - respirator wear time, which comfort governs, is the denominator any wearable PM exposure estimate in industry has to account for.

PAPERS.title: Meteorology-Driven Partitioning of Emerging Contaminants between PM2.5 and Coarse PM10-2.5 Aerosols
PAPERS.short: Guanzhong Plain paired PM2.5 coarse PM10-2.5 emerging contaminants UHPLC-MS/MS meteorology (abstract truncated)
PAPERS.pm: Metadata only - paired PM2.5 and coarse PM10-2.5 filter samples analysed for emerging contaminants
PAPERS.endpoint: Metadata only - size partitioning of emerging contaminants with meteorology
PAPERS.affil: not stated in record
PAPERS.n: Metadata only: the Crossref record carries only a two-sentence fragment. It states that paired PM2.5 and operationally separated coarse PM10-2.5 samples from the Guanzhong Plain were analysed by UHPLC-MS/MS for atmospheric emerging contaminants, and that partitioning between fractions shifts with weather. No result is retrievable and no finding is asserted here. Relevance: indirect - size partitioning that moves with meteorology is a reason fixed PM2.5/PM10 ratios in sensor correction models fail.
